name: Set 8: Karoo Nights & Cold Pints
description: Cricket Icons, Classic Sitcoms, Smoked Meats & Historic Battles

questions.q: What is the standard metric boiling point of water at sea level?
questions.fact: 100°C (212°F) at standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.q: In a deck of cards, how many Queens are there in total?
questions.fact: One Queen in each of Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades.

questions.q: What color jersey is awarded to the overall leader of the Tour de France cycling race?
questions.fact: The iconic yellow jersey worn by the general classification leader.

questions.q: What popular South African non-alcoholic malt beverage is brewed with barley and hops and marketed as an energy restorer?
questions.fact: South Africa's first homegrown 0.0% alcohol beer.

questions.q: What is the capital city of the Netherlands, famous for its canals and bicycles?
questions.fact: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital, while The Hague houses government.

questions.q: How many players are on the ice for one team at full strength in an ice hockey game?
questions.fact: 5 skaters plus 1 goaltender.

questions.q: Which gas do plants absorb from the air to perform photosynthesis?
questions.fact: Plants take in CO2 and release O2.

questions.q: What is the name of the green-skinned, pear-shaped fruit whose flesh is the main ingredient in guacamole?
questions.fact: Avocados (avocado pear).

questions.q: In a standard game of chess, which piece can only move diagonally across the board?
questions.fact: Bishops move any number of squares diagonally on their starting color.

questions.q: Which popular South African fast-food chain, founded in 1967, is famous for its Mega Rib Burger, thick milkshakes, and breakfast plates?
questions.fact: Wimpy opened its first South African restaurant in Durban in 1967.

questions.q: In the 1992 Cricket World Cup in Australia, which South African fielder produced the most iconic flying run-out in history by diving headfirst into the stumps to dismiss Inzamam-ul-Haq?
questions.round: Round 2 · Proteas Cricket & Global Cricket Icons
questions.fact: 8 March 1992 in Brisbane: Jonty was airborne horizontally when he shattered the stumps.

questions.q: Who was the first South African batsman to score a triple century (311 not out) in Test cricket, achieving the feat at The Oval against England in 2012?
questions.round: Round 2 · Proteas Cricket & Global Cricket Icons
questions.fact: Hashim Amla batted for over 13 hours to score 311*.

questions.q: Which South African fast bowler was nicknamed 'White Lightning' for his terrifying 150 km/h bouncers in the 1990s?
questions.round: Round 2 · Proteas Cricket & Global Cricket Icons
questions.fact: Allan Donald took 330 Test wickets for South Africa.

questions.q: In cricket, how many runs is a 'century'?
questions.round: Round 2 · Proteas Cricket & Global Cricket Icons
questions.fact: A century is 100 runs.

questions.q: Which legendary Australian leg-spinner took 708 Test wickets and bowled the 'Ball of the Century' to Mike Gatting in 1993?
questions.round: Round 2 · Proteas Cricket & Global Cricket Icons
questions.fact: Shane Warne: 'The King of Spin'.

questions.q: Which cricket ground in Cape Town is famed for its lush grass embankments, oaks, and stunning backdrop of Devil's Peak and Table Mountain?
questions.round: Round 2 · Proteas Cricket & Global Cricket Icons
questions.fact: Widely regarded as one of the most picturesque cricket venues in the world.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of fielders permitted outside the 30-yard fielding circle during the first 10 overs of a men's ODI powerplay?
questions.round: Round 2 · Proteas Cricket & Global Cricket Icons
questions.fact: Only 2 fielders outside the circle during Powerplay 1 (overs 1-10).

questions.q: Which South African wicketkeeper-batsman captained the Mumbai Indians and held the record for most dismissals by a keeper in Test history (555 dismissals)?
questions.round: Round 2 · Proteas Cricket & Global Cricket Icons
questions.fact: Mark Boucher took 532 catches and 23 stumpings in 147 Tests.

questions.q: What is the international biennial Test cricket series played between England and Australia called?
questions.round: Round 2 · Proteas Cricket & Global Cricket Icons
questions.fact: Contested for a tiny terracotta urn supposedly containing the ashes of a cricket bail.

questions.q: Which South African left-handed opener batted through all five days of a test match and later coached India to the 2011 World Cup title?
questions.round: Round 2 · Proteas Cricket & Global Cricket Icons
questions.fact: Gary Kirsten played 101 Tests and coached India to World Cup triumph.

questions.q: In the legendary British comedy Fawlty Towers, what was Basil Fawlty's strict instruction to staff regarding his visiting German guests?
questions.fact: 'Don't mention the war! I mentioned it once, but I think I got away with it!'

questions.q: In the American version of The Office, who is the eccentric, beet-farming Assistant to the Regional Manager?
questions.fact: Dwight Kurt Schrute III, owner of Schrute Farms B&B.

questions.q: Which British comedy troupe created Monty Python and the Holy Grail and Life of Brian?
questions.fact: John Cleese, Michael Palin, Terry Jones, Eric Idle, Graham Chapman, and Terry Gilliam.

questions.q: In the classic comedy sitcom Blackadder, what was Baldrick always famous for having?
questions.fact: 'I have a cunning plan, my Lord!'

questions.q: What is the name of Homer Simpson's long-suffering wife with the towering blue beehive hair?
questions.fact: Marjorie 'Marge' Simpson (née Bouvier).

questions.q: Which British sitcom set in Peckham followed market trader Derek 'Del Boy' Trotter trying to become millionaires?
questions.fact: 'This time next year, Rodney, we'll be millionaires!'

questions.q: In the 2004 comedy Anchorman, what musical instrument does Ron Burgundy play during his jazz club solo?
questions.fact: Ron Burgundy's fiery jazz flute solo.

questions.q: Which South African stand-up comedian became the global host of The Daily Show in New York from 2015 to 2022?
questions.fact: Trevor Noah hosted the acclaimed satirical news show on Comedy Central.

questions.q: In the sitcom Friends, which character was notoriously married and divorced three times (Carol, Emily, Rachel)?
questions.fact: Ross Geller: 'The Divorce Force'.

questions.q: Which South African comedian is affectionately known as 'The Cousin' with his famous stand-up routines about Nou Gaan Ons Braai?
questions.fact: Barry Hilton: iconic face of South African comedy for over 30 years.

questions.q: What inert gas is used alongside carbon dioxide to give draught Guinness stout its creamy head and smooth texture?
questions.fact: Nitrogen creates smaller, tighter bubbles for the famous cascading surge.

questions.q: What type of vinegar is traditionally preferred when curing traditional South African biltong?
answers: Brown spirit vinegar or malt vinegar
questions.fact: Brown vinegar or malt vinegar imparts mellow acidity without bleaching the meat.

questions.q: What cut of lamb from the loin or rib is cut with the bone in and braaied hot and fast for tender perfection?
questions.fact: Tjops on the braai: crisp up the fat strip first, then sear the meat.

questions.q: What is the main aromatic flavoring component in classic London Dry Gin?
questions.fact: By legal definition, gin must have a predominant flavor of juniper.

questions.q: What spicy North African paste made from red chili peppers, garlic, and caraway is popular as a braai marinade?
questions.fact: Harissa originated in Tunisia.

questions.q: What is the traditional name for the large clay beer pots used in Zulu culture to serve traditional umqombothi sorghum beer?
questions.fact: Ukhamba: spherical earthenware beer vessel shared among guests.

questions.q: What classic South African dessert consists of small, fluffy dumplings poached in spiced cinnamon syrup?
questions.fact: Souskluitjies: warm cinnamon sugar dumpling comfort food.

questions.q: What is the German term used for bottom-fermented beers that are stored and conditioned at cold temperatures for weeks?
questions.fact: 'Lagern' means 'to store' in German.

questions.q: Which South African wine estate in Constantia, founded by Simon van der Stel in 1685, produced sweet wines favored by Napoleon Bonaparte on St Helena?
questions.fact: Groot Constantia is South Africa's oldest wine-producing estate.

questions.q: What South African biscuit is shaped like a small tartlet, filled with apricot jam, and topped with a baked coconut meringue cap?
questions.fact: Named in honor of Prime Minister J.B.M. Hertzog.

questions.q: In which province was the historic 1879 Battle of Isandlwana and the defense of Rorke's Drift fought between the British Army and the Zulu Kingdom?
questions.fact: In the rolling hills of Zululand, KwaZulu-Natal.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Greece, considered the cradle of Western civilization and democracy?
questions.fact: Athens, home of the Acropolis and Parthenon.

questions.q: What is the oldest surviving colonial building in South Africa, constructed by the Dutch East India Company between 1666 and 1679 in Cape Town?
questions.fact: A five-pointed star fortress in the heart of Cape Town.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Scotland?
questions.fact: Edinburgh, dominated by Edinburgh Castle.

questions.q: Which South African general and statesman served as Prime Minister, helped draft the UN Charter, and was a member of the British Imperial War Cabinet?
questions.fact: Jan Christian Smuts: philosopher, botanist, and military commander.

questions.q: What is the longest artificial structure ever built by human civilization, stretching thousands of kilometers across northern China?
questions.fact: Over 21,000 km in total length including all branches.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Switzerland?
questions.fact: Bern acts as the de facto federal city (capital) of Switzerland.

questions.q: Which famous French military leader was defeated at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815?
questions.fact: Defeated by the Duke of Wellington and Field Marshal Blücher.

questions.q: What river flows directly through the city of Paris, France?
questions.fact: The Seine River divides Paris into the Left Bank and Right Bank.

questions.q: In which Free State town was the National Museum founded, famous for its Florisbad skull archaeological discovery?
questions.fact: The Florisbad skull was discovered in 1932 near Bloemfontein.

questions.q: In what calendar year did the historic Battle of Blood River take place in KwaZulu-Natal?
questions.fact: 16 December 1838.

questions.q: How many total balls did Hashim Amla face when he scored his historic 311 not out at The Oval in 2012?
questions.fact: Amla faced 529 balls across 790 minutes of batting.

questions.q: In what calendar year did construction of the Castle of Good Hope in Cape Town begin?
questions.fact: Started in 1666 and completed in 1679.
